name: Firan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference list for fira1238 (11 references: Blench 2006 Izere items, Blench 2008, Decker et al. 2021, Blench 2024, Shimizu 1975, Blench 2011 Atlas, Ethnologue 16, Blench 2002 Ogmios, Blench 2006 'strange case of Ganang')
sources.note: Bibliographic only; the three Glottolog refs typed grammar_sketch/dictionary (Blench 2006) are Fobur Izere items, not Firan.
Tertiary. Consonant table credited to Decker et al. 2021; tone paragraph credited to Blench 2024: five tones (H, M, L, rising, falling). No mention of stress. Not used as a statement.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Benard Abraham, John Muniru & Julius Dabet. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Firan [fir] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-002. Dallas: SIL International. 46 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Section 6.2 (p. 10) compares Firan and Izere consonants and vowels and says on tone: Blench (2019:10) gives Izere five tones (three level, two contour); Blench's Firan paper makes no statement about tone but a scan of his wordlist reveals a similar five-tone system; the SIL wordlists did not mark tone often enough to make a statement. Appendix D (p. 29): transcriptions preliminary, no in-depth analysis of tones. Direct SIL PDF is behind a Cloudflare JS challenge from our machine; copy taken from the Wayback Machine snapshot of 2024-11-15.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2008. The Fəran language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 25 April 2008. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 24 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 3 Phonology (p. 2) has 3.1 Vowels, 3.2 Consonants and a heading '3.3 Tones' with no text under it; the wordlist entries are tone-marked (e.g. kuyák, kutá) but the paper contains no statement on tone, stress or accent. Live rogerblench.info returns 403 to this host; copy taken from the Wayback Machine snapshot of 2025-05-28.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. Introduction to a preliminary dictionary of the Fɨran language of Central Nigeria. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 21 pp.

sources.note: The only first-hand phonological write-up of Firan with a tone analysis (Wikipedia reports five tones H/M/L/rising/falling from it); a dictionary introduction of this kind by Blench normally has a phonology section that would also be the place for any remark on stress. Not on Wayback; rogerblench.info and academia.edu both refuse this host.

sources.note: Closest relative (Izere, same Izeric group); Decker et al. 2021 cite its p. 10 for the five-tone system they project onto Firan. Would show what Blench says about tone vs. stress in the Izeric group, but it describes a different language, not Firan. Wayback snapshot exists (2021-04-18) but was not fetched sources because it is not a Firan source.
